title: The augmented bounded-below injective bicomplex total is a K-injective resolution
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $K$ be a bounded-below cochain complex. Let $I^{s,r}$ be a double complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] with complex degree $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution degree $r\in\mathbf N$, and let $a:K\to I$ be a bicomplex augmentation from $K$ concentrated in resolution degree zero. Assume that there is $b\in\mathbf Z$ with $I^{s,\bullet}=0$ for $s<b$, every $I^{s,r}$ is injective, and each $a^s:K^s[0]\to I^{s,\bullet}$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Extend resolution degree by zero and flip as in [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], obtaining $J$ with indices $(r,s)$. Then there is a quasi-isomorphism $\epsilon:K\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)$ whose degree-$n$ component is $a^{n,0}$ followed by the extension identification and the inclusion of the $(0,n)$ summand. The total complex is K-injective [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. No conditions on the horizontal cycles, boundaries or cohomology are required.

proof.text: Define f_n to be the specified map into the (0,n) summand. Expand the total differential using ι_D₁, ι_D₂, d₁_eq, and d₂_eq. The resolution term vanishes by (a.f n).comm 0 1, while the complex-degree term equals d_K followed by f_{n+1} by a.comm. Both total signs in resolution degree zero are one. These equations construct the chain map aug with the required components.
Apply [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-augmentation-quasi-iso] to this explicitly constructed aug, its component equation, hbelow and hrows.

Choose the lower bound b. Extension gives zero summands when r<0, and hbelow gives zero summands when s<b. A diagonal r+s=n below b is therefore all zero; coproduct hom_ext proves strict lower boundedness of the total. In degree n form CoreHasTotal with index set {s in Z | b≤s≤n}, φ₁(s)=n-s and φ₂(s)=s. Every omitted summand is zero. Transfer the given injectivity to each finite summand through extendXIso, then transfer injectivity of its finite biproduct through biproduct.isoCoproduct and the unique colimit-point isomorphism. Apply the Mathlib bounded-below-injectives theorem to this total.
